THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the judgment and award dated 22.07.2019 passed in MVC No.3061/2018 by the Court of Small Causes & Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (SCCH-9) (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal').
2. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2- Insurance Company.

sentences.text: 3. The status of the parties before the Tribunal is retained for the sake of convenience.

4. The case of the appellant/claimant is that he filed a claim petition before the Tribunal under Section 166 NC: 2024:KHC:21434 of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'M.V. Act') claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 20.04.2018, when the petitioner was riding the Suzuki Access bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EH-6791 near RV Engineering College, Kengeri, at that time the driver of the car bearing No.KA-09-MA-7729 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner, due to which, the petitioner sustained grievous injures.

Immediately, the claimant was shifted to B.G.S.
Global Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient.

Due to the accidental injuries,
he has suffered from disability.
Therefore, the claimant filed the petition seeking compensation on various grounds.

5. Respondent No.2-Insurance Company appeared before the Tribunal and filed written statement and denied the petition averments and also disputed the manner of accident, age of injuries,
occupation including NC: 2024:KHC:21434 the income and disability suffered by the petitioner and prayed for dismissal of the suit.

sentences.text:
On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed the following issues for consideration:
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 20.04.2018 at about 1.15 p.m., when petitioner was riding the Suzuki Access bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EH-6791 on the left side of the road by observing the traffic rules and when he reached near RV Engineering College, Kengeri, Bengaluru, at that time all of a sudden on a car bearing Reg.No.KA-09-MA-7729 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life with high speed and dashed against the petitioner's scooter.
Due to the impact the petitioner fell down along with vehicle and sustained injuries all over the body?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What Order?

7. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1, the doctor was NC: 2024:KHC:21434 examined as PW.2 and the Assistant Manager of BGS Hospital was examined as PW.3 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P20.
The respondents have not led any evidence.

8. On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal answered issue No.1 in the affirmative and issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and the tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.5,20,000/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization and also held respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the claimant and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of two month from the date of award.
9 . Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court challenging the impugned judgment and award.
It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the Tribunal has committed an error in considering the income of the petitioner as Rs.8,000/- p.m. which is meager.
Even in the Lok-adalath, for the accident occurred in the year 2018, Rs.12,500/- p.m. has considered as notional income.

Apart from that the tribunal awarded meager amount towards 'pain and suffering', 'attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance expenses' for 24 days and also awarded meager compensation on other heads.
Hence, he seeks enhancement of compensation and prays to allow the appeal.
11. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company justified the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
However, he fairly admits that Rs.12,500/- could be considered as notional income of the petitioner in the absence of the documents.
Therefore, on these grounds, he seeks dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text: Having heard the learned counsel for appellant- claimant and the learned counsel for respondent-Insurance Company, on perusal of the Exs.P1 to P20, the point to be considered is as to whether the tribunal has committed an error in calculating the income of the petitioner as Rs.8,000/- p.m. is meager and awarded lesser compensation for the injuries sustained by him which requires for enhancement.
13. On perusal of the records, the accident was occurred on 20.04.2018 at about 1.15 p.m., due to rash and negligent act of driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA- 09-MA-7729.
Respondent No.2 also did not challenge any liability fixed on the insurance company.

Therefore, the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal in this regard that the petitioner/claimant was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. as was working as electrician and no documents produced except this oral testimony.

Therefore, the Court required to consider the notional income of the petitioner for the accident occurred in the NC: 2024:KHC:21434 year 2019 as Rs.12,500/- p.m. considered in the Lok- adalath as notional income.
Therefore, I will consider Rs.12,500/- p.m. as income instead of Rs.8,000/- p.m. awarded by the tribunal.
14. As regards the injuries sustained by the petitioner was grievous in nature, he was suffered various fractures and underwent surgery twice.

He has admitted in the hospital and sustained fracture of D12-L1-L2 fusion with L1 and partial D12 and also injuries on left rib, such being the case, granting of Rs.50,000/- against pain and suffering is meager.
Hence, I propose to increase 'Rs.75,000/-' towards 'Pain and suffering' instead of 'Rs.50,000/-' awarded by the tribunal.
15. As regards the disability, the tribunal has considered 4 months of laid up period by taking income of Rs.8,000/- p.m.
The doctor has stated 30% of the disability towards whole body.
However, the tribunal considered 20% of the disability.
In my opinion, 20% to whole body is appropriate and need not be enhanced.
If NC: 2024:KHC:21434 notional income of the petitioner is Rs.12,500/- and the age of the petitioner is 41 years, the multiplier applicable is '14'.

Therefore, the 'loss of future income' would be calculated as Rs.12,500/- X 12 X 14 X 20% = Rs.4,20,000/-.
16.
As regards 'attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance expenses', the tribunal awarded Rs.20,000/-.
As the petitioner admitted twice in the hospital for more than 24 days, he could have spent huge amount towards 'attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance expenses'.
Hence I propose to award Rs.40,000/- towards 'attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance expenses' instead of Rs.20,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
17. As regards laid up charges, the tribunal considered Rs.8,000/- for 4 months is meager.
Hence, I propose to award Rs.12,500/- x 4 = Rs.50,000/- under the head of 'loss of laid up period'.

4 18.
As regard the medical expenses, the tribunal awarded Rs.59,000/- is retained.
19. As regards the loss of future amenities, the tribunal awarded Rs.50,000/- is retained.

20. With regard to future medical expenses, the tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, which is just and proper and the same remains unaltered.
21.
In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,34,000/- as against Rs.5,20,000/- as mentioned in the table below:

Heads Amount in  Rs.
Towards pain and suffering 75,000-00 Towards attendant charges, extra nutritious 40,000-00 food and conveyance expenses Towards loss of income during laid up 50,000-00 period Towards Medical expenses 59,000-00 Towards loss of future income due to 4,20,000-00 permanent disability
Towards loss of future amenities and 50,000-00 happiness
Towards future medical expenses 40,000-00
